question: Will no qualifying diplomatic US-Iran meeting occur by September 30, 2026?
rules:
On June 22, the first round of U.S.-Iran diplomatic talks in Switzerland concluded, with mediators reporting progress toward a roadmap for a final deal and follow-on technical talks expected to continue (see: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/6/22/us-iran-agree-on-roadmap-towards-final-deal-in-switzerland-talks).

This market will resolve according to the country in which the next formal senior-level round of peace talks between representatives of the United States and Iran begins by September 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

A qualifying round must be a deliberate in-person diplomatic meeting or negotiating round concerning US-Iran relations, involving senior representatives of both the United States and Iran who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to conduct or materially direct diplomacy on behalf of their governments.

Indirect in-person diplomacy through designated mediators, facilitators, or interlocutors will qualify, provided senior representatives of both the United States and Iran are participating in the same formal diplomatic process with the knowledge and authorization of their respective governments. evidence.publisher: Reuters, via The Times of Israel
evidence.excerpt: Qatar is working with partners in the region and around the world, including China, to resume talks between the United States and Iran, a Qatari foreign ministry spokesperson said. Qatar’s prime minister and foreign minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani, was leading a delegation in Beijing.

evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan
evidence.excerpt: Japanese Foreign Minister Motegi Toshimitsu held a telephone call with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on September 8. Motegi expressed concern about renewed exchanges of attacks between the United States and Iran, called for talks to resume as soon as possible, and requested Iranian flexibility to avoid prolonging the impasse. Both ministers agreed to maintain close communication toward a diplomatic resolution.

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War and Critical Threats Project
evidence.excerpt: In its September 8 update, the Institute for the Study of War and Critical Threats Project reported nothing significant under its US-Iran negotiations section.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said contacts with regional countries to defuse the war were continuing and described meetings with a visiting Qatari delegation as good. He also said negotiations with Oman over a temporary safe transit route through the Strait of Hormuz were making significant progress. Baghaei blamed Washington for breaching the earlier memorandum of understanding and attributed insecurity in the strait to US attacks and the naval blockade.

Vice President JD Vance said the United States was not talking to Iran and would not do so unless Iran stopped shooting at commercial shipping. He presented an end to those attacks as the condition for resuming negotiations.

CNN reported that US-Iran talks had stalled and that the White House had said the preceding Thursday that no negotiations were ongoing. Iran and Oman continued discussions on an arrangement to restore maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, with regional mediators including Qatar backing those discussions. Iranian officials linked navigation through the strait to broader discussions with Washington and regional security developments.

evidence.publisher: Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs
evidence.excerpt: Switzerland welcomed progress during diplomatic talks involving the mediators, Iran and the United States at the Bürgenstock overnight on June 21–22. It welcomed the establishment of a high-level committee and a roadmap targeting a final agreement within 60 days. The roadmap provided for the immediate resumption of technical discussions.
